prompts.zebra:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: original complete-body sprite animation drawings for a toddler wildlife game. Image 1 is the EXACT character, rendering style, facial identity, body proportions and facing reference. Image 2 is ONLY a gait planning diagram, never copy its colors, shapes, labels or line-art style. Create ONE transparent sprite sheet, exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, EIGHT complete drawings in the same numbered order as Image 2. SAME stationary camera and SAME horizontal body size, identical torso/head location in every cell, generous empty margins, single flat common ground baseline. Face LEFT in a side view with slight three-quarter depth so all FOUR legs are always separately readable; far legs naturally a little darker. Render the entire original character in every frame, not separated limb parts.

PRIMARY GOAL: NORMAL FOUR-BEAT WALK, NOT TROT OR RUN. The left and right BACK legs must genuinely alternate and swing a full visible stride; never glue the rear pair together or leave both rear feet unmoving. Three feet bear weight while one foot swings. Front legs also alternate; never lift both front feet together. Hip/stifle/hock joints have correct quadruped anatomy, knees and heels are not reversed. Each drawn foot must connect to its own full limb, four legs and four hooves in EVERY frame, no hidden missing legs.

Ordered poses:
1 near hind hoof at rear just starting toe-off; far hind planted in midstance; both front hooves planted.
2 near hind leg bent and hoof AIRBORNE under belly clearly ADVANCING LEFT; far hind planted; both front hooves grounded.
3 near hind hoof has LANDED FORWARD left of its hip, bearing weight; near front toe starts to lift from trailing position.
4 near front hoof AIRBORNE advancing left ahead of chest; both hind feet are grounded at different stride positions.
5 near front hoof lands forward; far hind starts toe-off from trailing rear position; near hind firmly grounded.
6 FAR HIND leg is bent and its hoof AIRBORNE advancing LEFT under belly; NEAR HIND is grounded further BACK to the RIGHT. Both front feet support. This back-leg contrast MUST be very clear.
7 far hind hoof lands FORWARD to LEFT of near hind hoof, transferring weight; far front starts lifting from trailing position.
8 FAR FRONT hoof AIRBORNE advancing left; near front supports. Both hind feet support at different positions. Next frame wraps to pose 1.

Keep gentle friendly face, matte faceted semi-3D children's style exactly from Image 1. No photographs, detailed fur, extra clothing, extra body parts or new art style. Do not rotate or turn the character between poses. No hopping, both hind feet never fold together. True transparent alpha background. NO scenery, ground shadow, labels, text, boxes, guides, checkerboard or colored feet.
Character is the zebra in Image 1. Preserve its black-and-cream stripes, short upright mane and tail; slim striped rear legs and four dark hooves. Frame 2 must visibly lift one rear hoof; Frame 6 must lift the OTHER rear hoof. Image 2 is a planning aid only.
